newsitem.title: GERMANY: American targets Latam for ex-Germany U.S..
newsitem.headline: American targets Latam for ex-Germany U.S..

text.p: American Airlines said it plans to focus more on Latin America freight on its remaining two daily flights from Germany to the U.S..
The U.S. carrier said earlier it would drop its daily Boeing 767-300 flight between Frankfurt and Miami from June 1, with the loss of 10-15 tonnes of daily cargo capacity.
American's cargo sales manager Germany, Egon Wedde, said higher yield South America freight would take preference on the daily Frankfurt to Dallas and to Chicago 767-300 flights from June.
Wedde told Reuters in a telephone interview: "The decision (to drop Miami) affects our South America business severely.
"We saw this decision coming because the passenger side did not do so well but for cargo it was quite successful," he added.
American had average load factors of 86 percent on the Miami route with most freight heading for Latin American destinations, he noted.
Wedde said: "We have flights from Dallas to Brazil, Argentina and Chile which we will try to use for higher yield freight from Germany."
Air cargo rates to Latin America were far higher than to U.S. destinations and thus justified giving preference to South America freight where possible, he explained.
